clue.text: Cancel my working for plant

indicators.note: something working is in operation, moving about, so the letters are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone calls off an order because they are busy tending a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The cyclamen is a flowering plant with swept-back petals, often grown as a pot plant in winter.

clue.text: As one on the pitch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: together, acting all at once
second meaning: sounding the same musical note

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a sports field, as if a team plays as one; in music it is the height of a note, and voices at the same pitch sing together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means simultaneously in agreement, and in music describes parts sounding at identical pitch.

clue.text: Some ninety locals heading north to find follower

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, against the usual direction
only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run sitting inside it

parts.note: a run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Some locals, aged ninety, travel north in search of a disciple.
explanation.walkthrough: Read upwards, ninETY LOCAls gives ACOLYTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is an assistant or devoted follower, originally one attending a priest.

clue.text: Hydrocarbon on file in a ferment

indicators.note: a ferment is a state of agitation, so the letters are churned up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemical compound is recorded in the records while fermentation goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: An olefin, also called an alkene, is a hydrocarbon with a carbon-carbon double bond.

clue.text: Lie and get browned off here?

definitions.text: Lie and get browned off here?

parts.words: Lie and get browned off here?
parts.note: surface reading: a place to sulk, fed up, after telling a lie
setter's reading: a place where you lie down and your skin is literally browned

explanation.walkthrough: 'Browned off' is British slang for fed up; here it is taken literally as tanned, and 'lie' means recline, not fib.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanning bed is where people recline under ultraviolet lamps to darken their skin.

clue.text: Great success of Brown and Green, say, taking to the air first

indicators.note: this word says one piece is placed at the front, ahead of the other

parts.note: airborne, in flight
brown and green are examples of hues

explanation.surface: Two people named Brown and Green triumph, perhaps as pilots taking off.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown and Green look like surnames; 'say' marks them as examples of colours.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass with flying colours is an idiom for doing something with great success.

clue.text: Tense, but outlook could not be better

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a grammatical tense, as in 'will have done'
second meaning: what lies ahead is ideal

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious even though their prospects look wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as nervous, but it is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a verb form for actions completed by a later time, and literally a flawless prospect.

clue.text: Lass can refuse to develop confidence

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters grow into a different arrangement

parts.note: the thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl's ability to say no helps her grow in confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-assurance is trust in one's own abilities, the same poise as confidence.

clue.text: Taken from Christmas to Lent

indicators.note: the letters are lifted out of the words that follow

parts.note: a run of letters across the three words

explanation.surface: A period of the church calendar, running from Christmas to Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is christmaS TO LENt.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen means taken without permission, a past participle like 'taken'.

clue.text: Ring for help after boat has capsized?

definitions.text: Ring for help after boat has capsized?

parts.note: surface reading: telephone for rescue
setter's reading: a ring-shaped buoy thrown to someone in the water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a verb, to call; it is a noun, a buoyant hoop.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifebelt is a floating ring thrown to someone in the water to keep them from drowning.

clue.text: Six about to face unknown lady

indicators.note: one piece comes up against the other, placed just before it
turning about means facing the other way, so the numeral is written backwards

parts.note: Roman numeral for six
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A sixth person goes to meet a mysterious woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a woman's name, so it serves for a lady, as crossword setters often use.

clue.text: Out of uniform, samurai possibly one of three soldiers booked?

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of what remains
out of means without, so the letter standing for uniform is dropped

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A samurai in civilian clothes might be one of three soldiers in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Aramis is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers, alongside Athos and Porthos; 'booked' means appearing in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramis is one of the trio of musketeers in Dumas's novel, so a soldier found in a book.

clue.text: Musically challenged, fed a note to perform

indicators.note: performing means working on something, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poor musician is given a note to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tone-deaf cannot tell musical pitches apart, so is musically challenged.

clue.text: Installed in castle, a reed organ

indicators.note: something installed in is set inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: a run of letters across the words

explanation.surface: A reed organ has been fitted inside a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reed organ' reads as one instrument; organ alone is the definition. The run is castlE A Reed.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is the organ of hearing, a body part rather than a musical instrument.

clue.text: First opportunity

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a chance or vacancy

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase, a first chance, but are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening batsman or move comes first, and an opening is also a chance or available job.

clue.text: Get to island with two different kings

parts.note: I is a standard abbreviation for island
R for rex, Latin for king
K for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: Someone reaches an island accompanied by a pair of monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get to' reads as reach, but here it means annoy; the kings are two different abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To irk someone is to annoy them, as in 'it really gets to me'.

clue.text: Lift United with applause

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names
approval, acclaim

explanation.surface: A cheering crowd boosts a football team called United.
explanation.definitionFit: To upraise is to raise or lift up, so the verb matches 'lift'.

clue.text: Jumble of tea and chips in a mess

indicators.note: a mess is disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A messy cafe meal of tea and chips all mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche can mean a medley or hotchpotch of bits from various sources, so a jumble.

clue.text: Skilled performer not quite in charge

indicators.note: not quite complete means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: an entertainer on stage
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A talented entertainer is almost the one running the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistic means having creative skill, so it is an adjective close to skilled.

clue.text: Caught in lacy pants? Doubtful!

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are treated as a mess and rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone caught wearing lacy underwear meets a sceptical response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like underwear (British for knickers), but it is slang for rubbish, so an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynical person is distrustful and sceptical, so doubtful of others' motives.

clue.text: Hear about game banning outsiders? Cunning!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other
banning outsiders means barring the letters at both edges

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
the bat-and-ball game

explanation.surface: Someone is told to listen about a sport that excludes strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the court sense, to try a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Trickery is deceitful cleverness, a noun matching cunning used as a noun.

clue.text: Reportedly cold pepper

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so it is the sound of the word that counts

parts.note: cold, said out loud

explanation.surface: Word has it that a pepper is cold, a paradox for a hot spice.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilli is a hot pepper, the fruit of a capsicum plant.

clue.text: Come out east and join up

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
combine, unite

explanation.surface: Instructions to leave in an easterly direction and enlist.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view, an exact verb synonym.

clue.text: Father welcomes a time for mickey-taking

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: to father offspring, or a male parent
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Dad makes room for a moment of teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the mickey is British slang for teasing or mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is mockery using humour or exaggeration, so it is a kind of mickey-taking.

clue.text: Ignoring the odds, insult head

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered positions keeps only the evenly placed ones

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off long odds and insults the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a verb or a chief, but it is the noun for the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is informal slang for the head, as in 'use your nut'.

clue.text: Be right alongside one repeatedly making complaint

indicators.note: alongside means placed next to, so one piece follows straight after the other

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
Roman numeral for one
the four letters just built, written a second time

explanation.surface: Someone always siding with another person keeps on whingeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a disease caused by vitamin B1 deficiency, and complaint means an illness.

clue.text: Lunatic in French river, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the spelling may differ

parts.note: the Seine is the river through Paris, with in before it

explanation.surface: A madman is found in a river in France, so we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic as an adjective means mad or crazy, the same as insane.

clue.text: One travelling from pole to pole?

definitions.text: One travelling from pole to pole?

parts.words: One travelling from pole to pole?
parts.note: surface reading: an explorer journeying between North and South Poles
setter's reading: wooden posts that carry overhead cable for sending messages

explanation.walkthrough: The poles look like the Earth's; they are the posts along which old message cables were strung.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegraph wire is strung from post to post to carry signals, so it literally travels pole to pole.
